title_en: Get Like a Dragon: Infinite Wealth, Dead Cells, and More in August's Humble Choice
summary_en: Get hundreds of dollars worth of Steam games, including Like a Dragon: Infinite Wealth, in this August's Humble Choice.
body_en:
It’s the first Tuesday of a new month (in this case, August), which can only mean one thing: a new batch of Steam games is available for pennies on the dollar. That’s because the August 2026 Humble Choice lineup is now live. It’s a murderer’s row of good games, spearheaded by Like a Dragon: Infinite Wealth and Dead Cells. Normally, these games would cost around $218, but they're all available now for just $14.99. Let’s take a look a this month’s games.
In addition to the Yakuza followup RPG, you get the beat-‘em-up TMNT Shredder’s Revenge Ultimate Edition, Dead Cells with the Bad Seed DLC, and more.
Like a Dragon: Infinite Wealth is a turn-based RPG take on the long-running Japanese crime series. It’s actually the second game in the series in the JRPG mode, and according to our review , it tweaks the combat formula in a lot of smart ways to make it even more tactical and satisfying.
TMNT: Shredder's Revenge is a co-op brawler that’s just a ton of fun to play, whether you want to dig into the surprisingly deep combat system and maximize your damage output, or just button mash with glee. Dead Cells (which got a !) is an indie darling roguelike that was good enough to get the dev team the gig to make the first new Castlevania game in a dozen years .
Decktamer is a deck-builder meets monster-catcher spun up in a turn-based roguelike. Conquest Dark is a fast-moving action-RPG. Gatekeeper is a co-op-friendly roguelike. Pile Up! is a strategic building game, and Dark Envoy is a “guns n’ sorcery” cRPG.
All of the games come in the form of Steam codes, and as usual, you get a free month of IGN+ bundled in. Humble Choice members save up to 20% on Humble Store purchases, depending on how long you’ve been a member. It is a subscription, but you can cancel any time, including right after signing up and redeeming the games — they’re yours to keep forever.
A portion of Humble Choice proceeds go to charity; this month it’s Oceana , an organization dedicated to protecting the planet’s oceans.
